types.description: An absurd weapon authored by a player. Carries a hidden Rock/Paper/Scissors classification used for deterministic clash resolution, plus generated artwork.

properties.label: Weapon
properties.description: The free-text weapon authored by the owning player. Hidden from the opponent until the arsenal reveal, then public for the rest of the game.

properties.label: Matchup Class
properties.description: Hidden Rock/Paper/Scissors classification assigned by classifyWeapon at creation. Never shown to any player. Frozen for the game and read by the chaincraft:dominant-gamepiece mechanic to resolve each clash deterministically.

properties.label: Artwork
properties.description: Reference to the generated weapon artwork. Populated by illustrateWeapon at creation. Empty in engines without image generation — text play is unaffected.

types.description: Each player's workbench of blank weapons waiting to be authored. createWeapon fills the top blank, classifies and illustrates it, then moves it to the arsenal.
Each player's completed arsenal of three authored weapons. Revealed publicly at the arsenal-reveal ceremony; the per-round secret is which weapon a player selects.

The battlefield. Both players secretly move their selected weapon here each round (pieces hidden, count visible until both have committed). revealArena makes them public for resolution; the dominant-gamepiece mechanic compares them and they return home.

properties.description: The current battle round number. Written automatically by the battle loop's writeIterationTo binding — no manual set-state needed.
Number of rounds a player must win to claim the championship. Defaults to 2 (best of 3). Can be overridden at game start.

Player ID of the winner of the most recently resolved clash. Empty string means a tie (both weapons shared the same Rock/Paper/Scissors class). Written by the chaincraft:dominant-gamepiece mechanic's resolve effect (the owner of the winning weapon); read by resolveRound and updateScores.

Piece ID of the winning weapon from the most recently resolved clash. Empty on a tie. Written by the chaincraft:dominant-gamepiece mechanic alongside roundWinner; the player winner is simply this weapon's owner. Read by resolveRound so the narration can name and describe the victorious weapon.

Player ID of the overall game champion. Empty string while the game is in progress. Set by updateScores when a player reaches roundsToWin victories. The battle loop's endCondition checks this field. NOTE: This property is retained for the battle loop endCondition. Winner announcement uses game.winners (populated by the engine via winConditions.onVictory).

Set true by rollReversal before each clash (25% probability). When true, the narration builds a fake-out moment of dramatic tension before revealing the real (already-determined) outcome. Reset to false after each round.
Cumulative clashes this player has won. Incremented by updateScores when roundWinner matches this player. The game ends when this reaches roundsToWin.

effects.description: Read the top piece in the forge inventory's description property. Using the following archetypes, assign exactly one of rock, paper, or scissors to its rps property: heavy / blunt / overpowering -> rock; enveloping / clever / trapping / control -> paper; cutting / precise / fast / piercing -> scissors. Judge by how the weapon would actually behave, not by its literal material. Each weapon should have a distinct RPS class; no two weapons in the same arsenal can share the same class, so pick the value  that most closely aligns and has not been used yet in this arsenal.

effects.template: Your weapon "{{input.weaponDescription}}" has been forged and added to your arsenal. The crowd gasps at your audacity.

rules: Use obnoxious game-show announcer style — think a pro-wrestling hype man crossed with an infomercial host
Welcome both players by name with theatrical ceremony
Include at least one groan-worthy pun in the opening line
Set the tone: this is a battle of wit and absurdity, not skill
prompt.computation: Create a boisterous opening announcement welcoming both players to the Absurd Armaments arena and building excitement for the weapon creation phase. 2-4 sentences.

rules: Reveal both players' complete arsenals to the arena (public broadcast)
Use bombastic sports-commentator energy with dramatic pauses implied by em-dashes
Weave a groan-worthy pun or absurd observation into each weapon's reveal
Never disclose any weapon's Rock/Paper/Scissors class — you are not even given it; only the weapons in {{arsenals}} and their descriptions
Build anticipation for the first clash
prompt.computation: Both players have finalized their arsenals of three weapons each, now revealed in {{arsenals}}. Generate a dramatic public reveal announcing every weapon by name with colorful commentary, ending with a teaser for round one.

rules: The winner has ALREADY been decided deterministically — read it from {{roundWinner}}. An empty value means a tie. Never contradict it
The winning weapon is identified by {{winningWeapon}} — give it the spotlight by name; an empty value means a tie
Narrate the clash between the two weapons in {{arenaWeapons}}, naming both
If {{includeReversal}} is true, write 1-2 sentences of fake-out tension before the real outcome lands — the crowd thinks one player won, then the truth hits
prompt.computation: The two selected weapons are in {{arenaWeapons}} and the dominant-gamepiece mechanic has already set {{roundWinner}} (the winning player) and {{winningWeapon}} (the victorious weapon piece). Narrate the clash dramatically, consistent with that result (empty = tie), giving the winning weapon top billing. Put the narration in roundNarrative.

effects.description: If game.property.roundWinner is not empty, find the player whose ID matches game.property.roundWinner and increment their player.property.roundsWon by 1. If that player's roundsWon now equals game.property.roundsToWin, set game.property.gameWinner to game.property.roundWinner. If roundWinner is empty (tie), make no score changes.
Move every weapon currently in the arena back to its owning player's arsenal inventory, so each player's arsenal is whole again for the next round.

rules: Crown the champion with full game-show ceremony — confetti implied
Recap the final score and winning weapon that clinched it
Console the loser with a backhanded compliment
End with a bombastic sign-off catchphrase
prompt.computation: The battle is over and {{winners}} holds the winning player ID(s). Generate a glorious victory announcement celebrating the winner, recapping their performance, and bidding farewell to the arena audience.

actions.label: Create Weapon
actions.description: Forge one absurd weapon for your arsenal. Each player creates exactly three weapons during the creation phase. The more ridiculous, the better — its hidden combat class is judged from your description.

steps.label: Weapon Description
steps.validationMessage: Describe your weapon. Be creative — "stale toast", "existential dread", and "sentient spatula" are all valid weapons.

actions.label: Select Weapon
actions.description: Secretly send one weapon from your arsenal into the arena for this round's clash. Both players choose simultaneously; the picks stay hidden until both have committed, then are revealed together for resolution.
